title: Mod-6 Counter Without an Adder
constraints: A **Johnson (twisted-ring) counter** in 3 flip-flops: each enabled edge shifts left and feeds back the **inverted** MSB: `q <= {q[1:0], ~q[2]}`. From reset (000) it cycles 000 → 001 → 011 → 111 → 110 → 100 → 000 (period 6).
`tick = 1` (combinational) in state 100, the last state before wrapping. No `+`, `-` or `*` anywhere.
Bonus insight: every state is decoded by a single 2-input gate.
hints: It's a shift register with one inverter in the feedback path.
State 100 is the only one with q[2] = 1 and q[1] = 0: `tick = q[2] & ~q[1]`.
Johnson counters are glitch-free when decoded (only one bit changes per step), which makes them popular for clock dividers and phase generators.
